$comment: Curated learning resources per skill id, for the route-report PDF. HAND-WRITTEN ON PURPOSE — the model invents plausible course titles and dead URLs, and a broken link in a report someone trusted costs more than the course was worth. Only entries someone has actually verified belong here. `url` is optional: omit it rather than guess, and the report falls back to naming the platform and title so the reader can search. Ordered roughly by how often each skill appears as a gap across published routes (see the count in each entry). Skills with no entry fall through to the generic guidance, which is honest about being generic.

data-analysis.title: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
data-analysis.note: The default for a reason: ends in a portfolio case study, not a quiz.
data-analysis.artifact: a one-page analysis of a public dataset that ends in a recommendation someone could act on

sql.title: SQL Tutorial
sql.artifact: a repo of five queries against a public dataset, each answering a question a manager would actually ask

python.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
python.note: Free to read online. Task-shaped rather than syntax-shaped.
python.artifact: a small script that automates a task from your current job, with a README showing before and after

figma.title: Figma for Beginners
figma.note: From Figma themselves, which is the version employers assume you did.
figma.artifact: a rebuilt screen from a product you use daily, with your reasoning annotated in the file

project-management.title: Google Project Management Professional Certificate
project-management.artifact: a one-page project plan for something you actually shipped, with the risk log filled in honestly

agile.title: Professional Scrum Master I
agile.note: The assessment is what employers recognise; the reading is free.
agile.artifact: a written retro of a real project run as sprints: what the ceremonies caught, what they missed

data-visualization.title: Free Training Videos
data-visualization.artifact: one chart that replaces a table you currently send, with a note on what it lets the reader stop doing

data-visualization.title: Storytelling with Data (Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic)
data-visualization.note: The one book hiring managers in this space have usually read.

excel.title: Excel Video Training
excel.artifact: a workbook that turns a messy export into a clean report with one refresh

ab-testing.title: A/B Testing
ab-testing.note: Built with Google. Free and still the clearest treatment.
ab-testing.artifact: a written test design for a change you believe in: hypothesis, sample size, and what would prove you wrong

langchain.title: LangChain for LLM Application Development
langchain.note: Short course, ends with something running.
langchain.artifact: a small agent that completes a multi-step task with tool calls, with its failure modes documented

rest-apis.title: Postman Learning Center
rest-apis.note: Free, and the tool itself is what teams actually use.
rest-apis.artifact: a documented API wrapping something you built, with auth and honest error messages

qa-testing.title: Applitools Test Automation University
qa-testing.note: Free, taught by practitioners, certificate per course.
qa-testing.artifact: a test plan plus a bug report for a real product, written so a developer could reproduce it in one read

supply-chain.title: MITx MicroMasters in Supply Chain Management
supply-chain.note: Heavier than most on this list; it also carries the most weight.
supply-chain.artifact: a mapped end-to-end flow of a real product with the two bottlenecks priced

motion-design.title: Animation Bootcamp
motion-design.note: The standard reference in this field. Expensive; the free tutorials are substantial on their own.
motion-design.artifact: a 15-second animated piece for a real brand, posted publicly with a process breakdown

after-effects.title: After Effects Tutorials
after-effects.artifact: a title sequence or animated explainer, exported and public, with the project file structured for handoff

video-editing.title: Premiere Pro Tutorials
video-editing.artifact: a 60-second cut from raw footage, with the edit decisions written down

photoshop.title: Photoshop Tutorials
photoshop.artifact: a before-and-after retouch or composite set, with the layer structure a reviewer could open

revit.title: Revit Self-Paced Learning
revit.artifact: a small modelled building with a clean sheet set extracted from it

lean-six-sigma.title: Six Sigma Yellow Belt Certification
lean-six-sigma.note: Yellow belt is the honest entry point; green belt is what postings usually name.
lean-six-sigma.artifact: a mapped process from your current job with one measured improvement and its data

design-systems.title: Design Systems (Alla Kholmatova)
design-systems.note: Short, and the vocabulary in it is the vocabulary the postings use.
design-systems.artifact: a mini component library: five components, tokens, and usage rules someone else could follow

prototyping.title: Prototyping in Figma
prototyping.artifact: a clickable prototype of one flow, tested on two people, with what changed after

product-management.title: Product Management Foundations
product-management.note: Expensive and aimed at people already adjacent to the work.
product-management.artifact: a one-page opportunity assessment for a feature you would kill, and why

machine-learning.title: Machine Learning Specialization (Andrew Ng)
machine-learning.artifact: a trained model on a public dataset with an honest error analysis, not just the accuracy number

deep-learning.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
deep-learning.note: Free, top-down, you build something in lesson one.
deep-learning.artifact: a fine-tuned model with a write-up of what it gets wrong and where it should not be used

accounting.title: Introduction to Financial Accounting (Wharton)
accounting.artifact: a three-statement model of a small real business, with the assumptions listed

etl.title: dbt Fundamentals
etl.note: Free, and dbt is what the postings usually mean by 'modern ETL'.
etl.artifact: a dbt project over a public dataset: staged models, tests, and documentation

aws.title: AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials
aws.artifact: one small service deployed end to end, with the architecture drawn and the bill explained

azure.title: Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)
azure.artifact: a deployed endpoint with logging and a load-test note

gcp.title: Google Cloud Fundamentals
gcp.artifact: a small pipeline running on a schedule, with monitoring that would catch it failing

llm.title: ChatGPT Prompt Engineering for Developers
llm.artifact: a prompt-driven workflow that produces a repeatable output, with the eval notes that show it holds up
